speaker: Doctor
text: The arterial blood gas indicates respiratory acidosis with mild hypoxemia, and the chest X-ray findings of ground-glass opacity and air bronchograms are highly suggestive of a specific lung condition. Given your history, have you noticed any signs of cyanosis or grunting respirations, and what was the gestational age of the baby at birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical picture of a preterm infant (32 weeks) with ground-glass opacities and air bronchograms on chest X-ray, combined with respiratory acidosis, confirms this diagnosis.
